grammar.title: Future Continuous and Future Perfect
grammar.explanation:
The **future continuous** (**will be** + -ing) describes an action **in progress** at a time in the future. This time tomorrow, the carpenter **will be laying** a brick, and the CEO **will be checking** the new bathroom.

The **future perfect** (**will have** + past participle) describes an action **completed before** a time in the future. By Friday, Daniel **will have finished** his business plan, and by June he **will have been promoted**.

Use **by** and **by the time** for the future deadline. By the time the nurse checks his blood pressure, Daniel **will have put** a bandage on his cut and **will have eaten** from his bowl.

The **future perfect continuous** (**will have been** + -ing) says **how long** an action will have continued. By June, Daniel **will have been working** as a carpenter for ten years.

For negatives, use **won't be** and **won't have**. For questions, ask ***Will** you **be using** the bathroom?* or ***Will** they **have arrived** by eight?*

After **by the time**, **when**, **before** and **until**, use a **present** tense for the future. Say *By the time you **get** home*, not *will get*.
examples: *This time next week, we **'ll be lying** on a beach.* (in progress)
*I **'ll be waiting** for you at the station at 6.* (in progress)
***Will** you **be coming** to the meeting?* (polite question)
*I **'ll be passing** the post office anyway, so I can post your letter.* (normal plan)
*By the time we get there, the film **will have started**.* (completed before)
*I **'ll have finished** this book by Friday.* (by + time)

practice.q: Rewrite in the future continuous: At nine tomorrow, Daniel lays a brick. (this time tomorrow)
practice.a: This time tomorrow, Daniel will be laying a brick.

practice.q: Rewrite in the future perfect: Daniel finishes his business plan before Friday.
practice.a: Daniel will have finished his business plan by Friday.

practice.q: Complete: By the time the CEO arrives, the carpenter ___ (finish) the bathroom.
practice.a: By the time the CEO arrives, the carpenter will have finished the bathroom.

practice.q: Rewrite: In June, Daniel will complete ten years as a carpenter. (future perfect continuous, by June)
practice.a: By June, Daniel will have been working as a carpenter for ten years.
